answer: In an agent market trading marble, each seller identity must lock 100 copper coins for 30 days before accepting orders. The bond is returned afterward, so creating 1,000 eligible identities requires tying up 100,000 coins at once. Attackers can whisper plans among their agents, but coordination cannot reuse coins already locked to another identity. This makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and foregone returns, while leaving wealthy attackers possible.
